rules.description: Firebase / Google Cloud service account key file
rules.fix: A service account key gives admin access to your Firebase/GCP project and bypasses Security Rules. Delete the key in Google Cloud Console → IAM → Service Accounts, remove the file, and use Application Default Credentials or a secrets manager instead.
Anyone who knows this string can forge login tokens for any user. Read it from process.env (e.g. JWT_SECRET), generate a long random value, and rotate it — which logs everyone out.

rules.description: Secret in Angular environment file (bundled into the browser)
rules.fix: Everything in environment.ts — including environment.prod.ts — is compiled into the JavaScript every visitor downloads. Public config (Firebase apiKey, project IDs) is fine; secrets must move to a backend (Cloud Function / API) and be rotated.

rules.description: Secret baked into a Docker image (ENV/ARG)
rules.fix: ENV and ARG values are stored in the image layers and visible to anyone who can pull the image (docker history). Pass secrets at runtime (docker run -e / orchestrator secrets) or use BuildKit `--mount=type=secret` for build-time secrets, then rotate this one.

Config files (Spring application.properties/yml, docker-compose.yml, Rails database.yml, .ini) usually get committed. Reference an environment variable instead — ${DB_PASSWORD} in Spring/Compose, ENV['DB_PASSWORD'] in Rails — and rotate the value.
Move the value into an environment variable or a secrets manager and rotate it if it was ever committed.
If this is a credential, move it to an environment variable. If it's not, add a `keyguard:ignore` comment on the line.

rules.description: Secret-looking variable uses a browser-exposed prefix
rules.fix: Variables with NEXT_PUBLIC_/VITE_/REACT_APP_/EXPO_PUBLIC_ prefixes are baked into the JavaScript bundle that every visitor downloads. Drop the prefix, read it only on the server, and rotate the value.

rules.description: Supabase admin key referenced in client-side code
rules.fix: Admin keys must never reach the browser. Move this call into a server route/action (route.ts, a Server Action, or an Edge Function) and use the anon/publishable key in client code.

rules.description: Debug mode enabled in a production config file
rules.fix: Debug output can leak stack traces, env values and internal paths. Disable it for production.

rules.description: Firebase security rules allow anyone to write
rules.fix: Anyone on the internet can create, change or delete this data with just your public project config. Require auth and ownership, e.g. `allow write: if request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == userId;`, and test with the Firebase Emulator before deploying.

rules.description: Firebase security rules allow anyone to read
rules.fix: Unless this data is meant to be fully public, require auth: `allow read: if request.auth != null;`. Anyone with your (public) Firebase config can read everything this rule covers.

rules.description: Firebase "test mode" rule: database is open until a date
rules.fix: The default test-mode rule (`if request.time < timestamp.date(...)`) leaves the whole database open to everyone until that date — then breaks your app. Replace it with real auth-based rules before launch.

rules.description: Terraform state file in the project
rules.fix: terraform.tfstate stores every resource attribute in plain text, including database passwords and keys. Use a remote backend (S3 + encryption, Terraform Cloud, GCS), add *.tfstate* to .gitignore, and rotate secrets if it was ever committed.

rules.description: Environment file is committed to git
rules.fix: Run `git rm --cached {file}`, add it to .gitignore, and rotate every value in it — they are in your git history now (see --history).
Add `.env*` and `!.env.example` to .gitignore so the next `git add .` can't commit it.
Every value in this file is public to anyone with the repo. Rotate them all, then purge the file from history with git filter-repo or BFG.

rules.description: Scan stopped early: too many findings in this file
rules.fix: This is usually a generated or vendored file. Review it, then add it to .keyguardignore if it's safe.
